events.title: Co-op, Rebuilt
events.summary: Co-op has been part of Free Company for a while. Now it actually feels like one company run by two people. You see your partner is on the map, you share the decisions that matter instead of just watching them happen, and the whole campaign holds together from the first contract to the last siege. Pick the jobs together. Weigh in on every call: one of you proposes, you both have a say, and the host makes it final. events.title: Free Company on Steam Deck
events.summary: I'm a solo dev, and I've built and playtested Free Company on Steam Deck the whole way through, not bolted it on at the end. The controls, the on-screen text size, and the battle interface were all tuned on the device across a lot of Deck sessions. What that means for you:Full controller support out of the box. events.title: Demo Update
events.summary: Demo Update, and the Road to Launch The demo has been out a little while now, and watching people take up the seal and run their own company has been the best part of this whole project. Thank you to everyone who has played it, broken it, and sent me notes. Here is a demo update built straight from that feedback, plus a look at where the company goes next, because the demo was never the finish line. It was the first camp on a longer road. events.title: Demo Is Live!
events.summary: The Demo Is Out: Take the Seal Free Company's demo is live for Steam Next Fest. Download it, muster your band, and see if you've got the nerve to lead one. It's A.D. 997. No crown stands behind you, no levy raised by writ. Just a seal, a muster roll, and the contracts you're willing to take. You run the company: you hire the bands, march the roads, pick the fights, and live with what they cost. events.title: Five Days to the Demo
events.summary: Five Days to the Demo Hello, sellswords. The Free Company demo releases on October 7th. This week was all about polish, bug hunting and getting it ready, and that's how I'll spend every day until launch. Co-op is in the demoFor a while I wasn't sure co-op should be in the demo at all. Two players sharing one campaign across the internet is a lot that can go wrong, and I didn't want your first impression to be a dropped connection. After this week's testing, I'm happy with it. events.summary: The trailer is here. The first one that actually shows the company armed, animated, and led. If you've been pulling up a chair on the workbench these past months, this is the thing all of it was building toward.
